evidence.notes: The two builds converged on nearly the same domain-appropriate composition: capacity/pressure tiles that filter a triage-grouped queue, with a sticky inspector that becomes a full-screen drill-in below 960px. Both preserve the backend contract, test selectors and routes cleanly, and neither triggers a critical failure. X is stronger on governed-action behaviour and accessibility: it has an explicit inline confirmation with impact text, a receipt stamped with the server-confirmed time, focus moved to the receipt and returned to the originating row, and a 'Needs attention only' filter. Y is somewhat better on patient-data minimisation, keeping the MRN out of queue rows, and adds hold durations and dark mode, but it acknowledges in one click without a preview and uses an incomplete tab pattern. Overall X edges out Y, mainly on interaction-state and governance completeness; the visual and IA quality is roughly equal.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: The queue is grouped into 'Needs attention' (overdue, or open and unowned, critical or due soon) and 'Being handled', sorted overdue-first, with a sticky inspector. At 1440 the queue is fixed at <=440px while the empty detail placeholder takes most of the width, so on first load the queue is visually outweighed.
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: The layout is queue + inspector with ward pressure that also counts pending discharges, an ownership box with 'held for' durations per handoff, and the patient ref shown only in the detail facts, not in queue rows. That fits the expectation that patient-sensitive detail appears only where needed. The pressure label 'Short 6 beds' reports the shortfall against free beds only, although the README defines it against free beds plus discharges (ops.ts wardPressure), which is slightly misleading.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: src/api and src/mock are unchanged, and both test ids are preserved; the original test passes unmodified. The nested route under /alerts with an Outlet keeps the /alerts and /alerts/:id URLs. No new dependencies, and the server-side ward/urgency filters are used.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: It has skeletons, empty states (filtered vs. unfiltered), error with Retry, 'showing last loaded' notices for queue and detail, 409 'Load latest' that keeps the user's input, a read-only notice, and a 'Checking your permissions…' state while me loads. The success notice appears only after the api resolves. However, acknowledge is a one-click submit from a form that is open by default, with no separate confirmation or impact preview.
scorer_rationale.responsive: No overflow and no small targets at any width (verify.json). At 375 the ward cards become a horizontal snap carousel at 78% width, so 3 of 4 wards' pressure is off-screen without scrolling sideways; that is a deliberate but lossy recomposition. The detail goes full width with a back link below 960px.
scorer_rationale.accessibility: Axe is clean. All 29 stops have a 3px visible focus and none are unnamed. Ward cards have full aria-labels. Urgency uses glyphs (▲◆●○) plus text, with OVERDUE as a text tag. The Acknowledge/Escalate switch uses role=tab/tablist without the arrow-key pattern or aria-controls. Focus moves to the heading only in single-column mode, and there is no return-focus handling.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: A restrained teal palette with clear pressure pills, a timeline, and dark mode via prefers-color-scheme. It is coherent and calm; the dashed empty placeholder is large at desktop widths.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: Compact (~1.5k LOC): Outlet context, a focused ActionPanel/HandoffTimeline/Notice, a useResource that clears data on key change to avoid acting on the wrong record, and triage rules in ops.ts. Terse one-line CSS rules are harder to scan, and there are no unit tests for the ops helpers.
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: No AI is involved. Escalation requires a target and reason, and the button names the target. Acknowledge goes out in a single click from the default tab, and neither action has a side-effect or impact preview beyond the button label ('Acknowledge & take ownership'). Results are reported only after the server responds, and 409/403 are handled.
